01 — About

The developer
behind the night shift

raevtar
KEBUMEN, INDONESIA — GITHUB SINCE NOV 2017

raevtar builds the kind of software that lives underneath everything else: proxy controllers for OpenWrt routers, management dashboards for Quectel 5G modems, container orchestration for rooted Android, and ultra-lightweight control panels that run fully offline.

The recurring pattern is a refusal to accept bloat — single compiled Go binaries, embedded web UIs, zero-dependency shell toolkits, CGO-free builds. If it can run on a router with 128 MB of RAM, it probably should.

02 — Creative Process

From problem
to production

Five steps, one glowing path. Every project — from modem dashboards to LLM gateways — walks the same road.

01

Discover

Problem & Research

Start with the constraint, not the feature list. A router with 128 MB of RAM, a modem that only speaks AT commands, a phone locked behind root — the limits write the spec.

02

Design

Architecture & UI

Sketch the system before the screens: process boundaries, data flow, failure modes — then a UI that stays honest about what the machine underneath is doing.

03

Build

Go & Systems Code

Write it in Go, shell or TypeScript — compiled, CGO-free, dependency-light. One binary, embedded assets, nothing to install and nothing to phone home.

04

Polish

Motion & Interaction

Dashboards deserve craft too. Micro-interactions, live signal graphs, instant feedback — the interface should feel as fast as the binary behind it.

05

Ship

Release & Iterate

Publish it open, watch real hardware break it in new ways, fix, repeat. Seventy-nine repositories in, the loop is the product.
